fieldMarks: Adults 6.4-12.1 cm with a broad yellow to greenish-yellow or tan stripe from head to tail.
Stripe bordered on each side by a narrow black line that may break into dashes toward the tail; may have a row of dark spots down the middle.
Breeding males have whitish lower eyelid glands, a mental gland on the chin and cirri on the snout.
behavior: Sometimes active by day in shaded wet areas; apparently active throughout the year in most of its range.
Hides under objects in or near water and disperses into wooded uplands in wet, warm weather; aggregates in winter.
Feeds opportunistically on small invertebrates, mainly terrestrial insects; eggs are laid April-June on the undersides of submerged rocks, logs or plants.
habitat: Rocky brooks, springs and seepages; adults hide under objects in or near water.
range: Southern Quebec and eastern Ontario south to northern Virginia, eastern West Virginia and central Ohio, with isolated populations in southern Labrador.

lookalikes.name: Southern two-lined salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: 14 costal grooves rather than 15-16; ranges to the south.

lookalikes.name: Northern dusky salamander
